slides.texte_overlay:
quiet skills that make people
think you're a genius

summing up in one line

after a meeting, a video or a book, sum it up in a single sentence. people who can squeeze a long idea into one clear line always sound sharp and clear.

asking why twice

when someone explains something, ask why one more time than feels polite. the second answer is where the real understanding is usually quietly hiding.

saying i'm not sure

admit when you don't know, then say how you'd find out. calm uncertainty sounds far smarter than a confident guess, and people trust you far more for it.

knowing a bit of everything

knowing a little about art, history and science makes you sound brilliant in any conversation. a few minutes a day of curious learning adds up faster than you'd ever expect.

remembering a few numbers

learn a handful of useful numbers by heart: distances, dates, populations. one accurate figure in a conversation makes you sound instantly well informed.
